parameters.name: MHA_IAU1982
parameters.rationale: Greenwich hour angle over the explicitly named legacy IAU-1982 sidereal series, kept as its own name so the legacy route has vectors of its own instead of being a silent second answer (the same rule that named MOD_FK5/TOD_FK5).

parameters.name: LST_IAU1982
parameters.rationale: Local sidereal time over the same explicitly named legacy series.

parameters.name: BdotTOutgoing
parameters.rationale: The B-plane T component taken on the OUTGOING asymptote. BdotT/BdotR are defined on the incoming asymptote (arrival geometry); a departure analysis needs the same two numbers on the departure asymptote and must not silently reuse the arrival ones.

parameters.name: BdotROutgoing
parameters.rationale: The B-plane R component on the outgoing asymptote.

parameters.name: BVectorMagOutgoing
parameters.rationale: The B vector magnitude on the outgoing asymptote.

parameters.name: BVectorAngleOutgoing
parameters.rationale: The B vector angle on the outgoing asymptote.

parameters.name: RLAIncoming
parameters.rationale: Right ascension of the INCOMING asymptote. DLA/RLA are the departure (outgoing) asymptote's declination and right ascension; an arrival analysis needs the incoming pair by name.

parameters.name: DLAIncoming
parameters.rationale: Declination of the incoming asymptote.

parameters.name: GeocentricLatitude
parameters.rationale: Latitude measured from the body centre rather than from the ellipsoid normal. Latitude is geodetic; the two differ by up to 0.19 deg on Earth and a consumer that wants one must be able to ask for it by name.

parameters.name: RadialVelocity
parameters.rationale: Component of velocity along the position unit vector. Its zero IS the apsis condition, and a stopping condition needs it as a NAMED parameter with a goal of zero rather than as a locator with a hidden formula.

parameters.name: HorizontalFlightPathAngle
parameters.rationale: Flight path angle measured from the local HORIZONTAL rather than from the radius vector. The two differ by a right angle and both are in use; a consumer must be able to ask for the one it means.

parameters.name: AltitudeOfPeriapsis
parameters.rationale: Periapsis radius minus the body's equatorial radius. Distinguished from RadPer so a mission constraint stated as an altitude is not silently compared against a radius.

parameters.name: AltitudeOfApoapsis
parameters.rationale: Apoapsis radius minus the body's equatorial radius.

parameters.name: ArgumentOfLatitude
parameters.rationale: Argument of periapsis plus true anomaly: the angle from the ascending node, which stays well defined as the eccentricity goes to zero and the argument of periapsis does not.

parameters.name: EccentricityVectorX
parameters.rationale: Component of the eccentricity vector. The magnitude alone loses the periapsis direction, which is what a targeting goal on the apsidal line needs.

parameters.name: EccentricityVectorY
parameters.rationale: Component of the eccentricity vector.

parameters.name: EccentricityVectorZ
parameters.rationale: Component of the eccentricity vector.

parameters.name: SemiMinorAxis
parameters.rationale: Semi-minor axis; for a hyperbolic orbit it is the impact parameter that the B-vector magnitude equals, so the two can be cross-checked against each other.

parameters.name: HyperbolicExcessVelocity
parameters.rationale: Speed at infinity on an escape trajectory, the square root of the characteristic energy. Named because a launch or arrival requirement is stated in speed, not in energy.

parameters.name: BallisticCoefficient
parameters.rationale: Mass divided by the product of drag coefficient and drag area. Derived from stated properties rather than stated itself, so it cannot disagree with them.

parameters.name: AreaToMassRatio
parameters.rationale: Solar-radiation-pressure area divided by mass, the quantity a radiation-pressure model is parameterised by.

parameters.name: UT1ModJulian
parameters.rationale: Universal time as a Modified Julian Date. UT1 is the scale the Earth's rotation is measured in, so an analysis that reasons about hour angles needs the epoch in it.

parameters.name: UT1Gregorian
parameters.rationale: Universal time as a calendar instant.

parameters.name: GeocentricAltitude
parameters.rationale: Radius minus the body's equatorial radius. This is the quantity apsis detection is defined on: geodetic height over an oblate body varies about 21 km with latitude, which swamps the radial signal of a near-circular orbit and puts apoapsis and periapsis about 90 deg apart in true anomaly.
